reasoning: Deepseek's 'unsafe' verdict was based on misidentification of legitimate 2026 CVE patches as fictitious. Qwen's thorough review of all patches confirmed they contain valid security fixes without malicious code. PKGBUILD uses secure practices including PGP verification.
disagreement_analysis: Deepseek misinterpreted future-dated CVE patches as malicious due to incorrect temporal context (assumed 2025 when report is dated 2026). Qwen reviewed patch contents while Deepseek relied solely on filenames.
coverage_issues: Deepseek failed to review critical files: Only audited 2 files vs Qwen's 12, missing security patches like CVE-2026-28387.patch
Deepseek skipped all additional files after PKGBUILD verdict
false_positives: Deepseek's 'supply-chain attack' claim: Misidentified legitimate 2026 CVE patches as fictitious
learnings: Improve temporal awareness: Models must reference report dates when evaluating CVE years
Enforce patch content review: Never judge patches solely by filename/CVE year
Prevent premature termination: Continue file review even after one 'unsafe' finding
Prioritize build-impacting files: Focus on PKGBUILD, install hooks, and patches over archived files
